notes.title: Spring sale and a new pinball collection!
notes.content:
[b]Hello pinball friends![/b]

It's Spring Sale and all Malzbies Pinball Collection tables are 50% off.

But that's not all!

There will be a new Pinball Collection and the shop page for the new collection is live as of today!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30900379/a43f2a9b00e27b2b91acedc604189e3a2234a956.png[/img]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2821740/Only_Pinball/]Only Pinball[/url]

If you are interested in it, then take a look. I will regularly post the status of the game there (so follow the game or add it to your wish list if you want to stay informed).

[i]But why is there a new collection and why isn't it being expanded here?[/i]

Because I have higher hardware requirements for the new tables! 
The tables are designed much more elaborately and realistically and a DX12 capable graphics card is required (at least an Nvidia GTX 960).

I can't simply increase the values of Malzbie's Pinball Collection, which is almost 7 years old, because an update shouldn't result in the game suddenly not working properly anymore.

Of course, Malzbie's Pinball Collection will remain as it is and will continue to be maintained.

See you on the leaderboards!

notes.title: 5 years Malzbie’s Pinball Collection!
notes.content:
On October 27th, 2017, the collection with the first 3 tables was released.

That’s why there’s 50% off on all tables this week. 

I’m also taking this anniversary as an opportunity to write you what I’ve done in the last few years and what I want to do in the near future.

I’ve been working on my new game CAVATUS for the last 2 years and I’m very close to its release. Only a few more weeks until it’s out!
I could tell you now what kind of game it is, but since I already have a shop page installed, where a demo of the game is to be found, I’ll just give you the link to that page.
Maybe someone is interested in a game with airplanes and a lot of shooting. ːsteamhappyː

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1499710/Cavatus/]CAVATUS[/url]           

OK, the new game is ready. And now?
Well, now I have time for new projects. And I already have an idea what I want to do next. 

[b]But:[/b]

I would also like to do something with pinball games again. Pinball is my passion!

[b]So:[/b]

In addition to my new project, I will also create new pinball tables time and again. But they will not be included in this collection; there will be something new.
There will be no free pinball tables again either, but instead a demo for testing.
Because I can’t stand the guys who have 1000 free games of each genre and then think they must rate my game negatively, just because they don’t understand pinball at all!

Maybe I’ll offer some kind of Early Access, maybe a model with DLCs. Just wait and see.
In any case, I will no longer try to get the tables running on ancient computers. At some point, you have to keep up with the times or leave it.

So, now you know what to expect.

You are welcome to open a thread where you can create requests for new tables. Themes, technology, game modes… I’m open to any of your proposals.

Thanks to everyone who plays my games and gave constructive feedback, praise and suggestions for improvement. The pinball community is great!

And above all:
[b]Have fun! [/b]

notes.title: Slight adjustments on all tables and bug fixing.
notes.content:
Hi Pinball Players!

I’ve made some physical changes on all tables.
Some of the tables are a bit slower than before, some are a bit faster.
Some flippers, slingshots and pop-bumpers have new coils now.  ;)  Some are stronger, some are weaker.

I’ve added a metal shield on the left side of the right bumper on Sheriff. This makes the game a bit easier to play.

While playing, and I was playing a lot, I’ve found and fixed 3 minor bugs.

And one more thing!

I’ve set a fps. limit for playing without V-Sync. If you turn off V-Sync (F10 key to switch between on and off), you will have a maximum of 120 fps. This prevents the graphics card to run too hot if you have a powerful card.
If you’re using a weak card, it will run hot anyway. 
You don’t need to play without V-Sync, because the calculation is independent of the framerate. But if you turn off V-Sync, you will see more frames and the movement of the flippers and balls are a bit smoother.

Do what you want but have fun! ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Some adjustments and bug fixes.
notes.content:
As usually after a big update, there are some new bugs which must be fixed, and some adjustments must be done.
That’s what I have just finished!

[b]Playground:[/b]

I fixed a physics bug where the captive ball could escape.
I also added some seconds for the swing mission.

[b]Carnival:[/b]

I fixed a bug on carnival where a ball could become stuck in the can targets area.

[b]Time Flight:[/b]

I made some physical adjustments. The table is faster and more challenging now. 

[b]All pinball tables:[/b]

I added and tweaked some mechanical sounds.

Also, a player asked for diagonal nudging, so I implemented it.
Now you can nudge/tilt the tables diagonally if you press up and left or up and right at the same time.
And I really mean at the same time, because the movement is so fast that you only have a tenth of a second for the input.

Have fun!

notes.title: The new physics update is up!
notes.content:
Hi, Pinball Friends!

First, I want to say thank you for your comments and likes.
It’s nice to see that you want the upgrade the same way I do.

I’ve updated all tables and tested them extensively.

And this is what has changed:

On[b] all tables[/b], the ball will bounce a bit more than before. The flippers are bouncier, too, and they are a bit slicker. So, if the ball comes from a lane, the ball will overshoot the pressed flipper on most of the tables. 
But now you’re able to shoot the ball more precisely to any target.  The flippers have an acceleration, and you can regulate the power, e.g. if you only tap them.
I’ve also modified some things on the tables. See below:

[b]Sheriff:[/b]

This table is still one of the most difficult tables, because of its pop bumpers. But I’ve made a moveable center post. After you shoot into the bank building, the post will move up when the ball is released. It stays there for some seconds and goes back again. This prevents you from losing the ball through the flippers.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30900379/dfbfc76f942e83b2b4a86ebd9383385644529bdf.png[/img]
Overall the table is easier now.

[b]Playground:[/b]

The lanes and flippers are a bit lower now.
The difficulty is about the same, but it’s easier to hit the captive ball from the swing and the targets from the seesaw.
All other tables are more precise now. Some are a bit faster, some are a bit slower. But overall, the difficulty is the same.

Test it! You will recognize it. 

Have fun!

notes.title: A physical update is coming soon!
notes.content:
Hi pinball friends!

I just want to say that I’m working on a great physics update.
I never liked the behavior of the flippers, because they are too linear in their movement.  But I had no clue how to simulate it to make it like in the real world.
Until last week! 
I had a fantastic idea and tested it on the carnival table (because of its center post). 
If you press the button really short, you can do this:

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30900379/d26f23cbf09a23d96c89621ee8e945a8beff1b52.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30900379/d26f23cbf09a23d96c89621ee8e945a8beff1b52.gif[/img][/url]

It is a great improvement!

It's not only an update for the flippers. The balls and all materials will be updated, too. 
It feels more realistic and it’s easier to aim. Surely, it changes a lot. The ball movement is slightly different, everything is bouncier and a shoot with the flipper feels a bit slower than before. But it’s worth it!

Now I’m working on the tables. 4 tables are done, and the rest should be done by next week!

I like it! 
And I think you will like it, too!

Have fun!

notes.title: Summer Sale and Multiscreen Mode
notes.content:
[b] 25%[/b] discount on all tables.
And if you buy an all tables bundle, you will get an extra discount!

But that is not all! Now there is a multiscreen mode!

As you probably know, Malzbie’s Pinball Collection can be played in portrait mode. You must only change your graphics card options to portrait.

This is great for pinball cabinets!

So far, it has not been possible to show the DMD (score display) on a separate screen. If you wanted to show the back glass, you had to use a third-party software to do so.

From now on, you can show the DMD and the back glasses on different screens.
Both are scale able and moveable. Move the elements by drag and drop and scale them with your mouse wheel, when the pointer is over the object to be scaled.
The new positions and sizes will be saved automatically.
The back glasses are now within the game. 

But there are some limitations:

•	The multiscreen mode will only work in portrait mode.   
•	It will not work in fullscreen mode. But that is no problem. You will not see any frames.
•	To activate the multiscreen mode and set the screens for the elements, you must use start parameters. 
•	Screen 1 is always the playfield.

[h3]And this is how it works:[/h3]

If you use the following parameter to set the amount of displays, the multiscreen mode will be activated automatically:

[b]-displays 3[/b]

With the following parameter you set the screen where you want to see the DMD.

[b]-score 2[/b]

With the following parameter you set the screen where you want to see the back glass.

[b]-bg 3[/b]

If you want to hide the DMD frame, you can use this parameter:

[b]-frame no[/b]

If something went wrong and you want to reset all multiscreen settings, you can use this parameter:

[b]-reset yes[/b]

It will delete all saved positions and scales. Nothing else. But do not forget to remove the parameter after you used it.

Have fun!

notes.title: Face lifting, performance and more!
notes.content:
A new update is on hand and a lot has been changed.
I have spent last month improving and matching the individual tables.

All tables have an “Attract mode” now with all the lamps flashing nicely. This is not really important, but pretty! ːsteamhappyː

I have improved some of the graphics and have slightly changed some of the objects. 
I have been successful in increasing the performance of all tables. You should notice this especially on slower computers. But on the other hand, I had to slightly change my illumination model and make some improvements on the code. I have taken this opportunity to also create the possibility of adjusting the basic illumination of each table separately.

On many tables, I have adjusted the physics in order to be able to play more precisely and in order to get the behavior even more realistic.
Most of all, two of the tables have profited from this:
The balls of the TTFB table move a little slower now and bounce off the objects more than before.
The playing field of the Labyrinth table has been flattened by one degree. Moreover, the Eastern and Western ramps have been made a little flatter, too, which has reduced the gradient of these ramps by additional four degrees.

You will also notice slight changes on the other table. In general, it should be easier now to hit the targets and ramps.

Have fun!

notes.title: Version 1.5 - Many improvements!
notes.content:
[b]-Revised ball physics[/b]

The ball moves much more accurately, and this enables the player to hit goals more precisely now.
The spin of the ball is getting much better now, too, when it hits the edges or rubbers, sometimes even giving it a certain twist.

[b]-Better performance[/b]

I have made some adjustments on the illuminated areas and succeeded in reaching a considerably better performance in the first 3 tables.
Moreover, the delays sometimes occurring with slower computers when using the flippers should be gone now.

[b]-Performance test when the collection is started for the first time[/b]

When the game is started for the very first time, a hardware test is now executed and the graphic options are adjusted automatically on the basis of the values determined this way.

[b]-Graphic improvements[/b] 

There are more reflections from the surfaces now, even when “real-time reflections” is switched off. In some cases, the light of the illuminated areas has been changed.

[b]-Slight adjustments on the tables due to the improved physics[/b]

The forces of flippers, bumpers and slingshots were adjusted in all tables. This changes the play behavior a little bit.
In “the garden”, the upper left flipper has been changed as regards its maximum deflection. It is much easier now, to get the ball onto the right flipper and, thanks to this effect, the left flower may be reached much easier.

It would be great if you could test all the tables now and let me know how you like the new features. ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Pinballs at half price!
notes.content:
I have cut prices for almost all of my pinballs. Only “Mud Race” is not offered at the new price yet, because Steam has provided for a specific period of time between the publication of a game and a possible change of its price. As soon as this time has elapsed, the “Mud Race” table will be available at the new price, too. The 4 pinballs I am still planning to publish will then be offered at the new price right from the beginning.

You may probably wonder why I decided to do so.

The reason is that only few people were willing to pay the regular price for a table. Most people only bought my pinballs during discount campaigns. So I decided to adapt to the market and to offer the pinballs at a lower price right away.
Of course, this will lower my earnings, too, if the number of pinball friends does not increase, but to be honest:
Pinballs are not very popular and the community is rather small!

But don’t worry! I will definitely complete the collection and finish all pinball tables. It is possible, however, that the publication of the new tables will take a longer period of time, because I also have to start new projects now that will hopefully attract greater interest.

And finally I've added a menu page with the table rules. To be seen under "help" of each table menu. I'm sorry, but it's only in English and German by now. Spanish, French and Italian will follow soon. 

Have Fun!

notes.title: Portrait Mode added
notes.content:
Now it's possible to play in Portrait Mode.
If you rotate your screen orientation before starting the game, it will automatically switch to portrait mode.
But you always can switch between portrait and landscape by pressing the P Key or inside any menu.

Have Fun!

notes.title: Just a few days till release!
notes.content:
Hi!
In a few days time, Malzbie’s Pinball Collection will be released.
As you have probably seen on the shop’s website, the “Time To Fight Back” table is available in the Collection for free. All other tables, however, have to be paid and you can buy them in the shop as DLC. 
If you like the free table and you want to try your hand at one of the other tables, you can do that in the Collection, because each table may be tried out for 2 minutes. You can repeat the test games over and over, but after approximately 2 minutes the game will be stopped. This timeframe should be sufficient for you to get a first impression of the table. 
As soon as I will add a new table to the Collection, this will, of course, be available for testing as well. 
So, if you really love pinball games, please download the Collection and let’s see whether you like my pinball tables.
I shall be very happy if you actually like them, and then I hope, of course, that you will also buy one or the other additional table.
I shall be sorry if you don’t like them. But I thank you in advance for at least giving my Collection a chance. This is the reason why the first table is for free and the others may at least be tested before buying them. Fairness is a must!

Have fun!
Yours Andreas ‘Malzbie’ Knauf
